title: AODB Data Export — Malicious bcp.exe Activity Detected

fields.organization: North Coast Regional Airport Authority — IT & Cybersecurity
fields.location: AODB Server Room (Rack 3, Server Bay 7) — NCIA-PACS-CORE
fields.summary: During a forensic audit of the AODB server, traces of the database export utility (bcp.exe) were found running nightly for the past 90 days. Logs indicate full database dumps of flight operations data, including gate assignments, airline manifests, and passenger name records. Query patterns suggest the attacker extracted passenger PII for all flights over the past 90 days. No known legitimate use for bcp.exe exists in this context; the activity pattern matches known exfiltration behavior.

findings.notes: Executed 327 times between 02:15 and 02:30 UTC daily; last run 10/21/2026, 02:22
Database export logs show 90-day full dump cycles; no audit trail for export operations
Job name not found in scheduled task list; appears to be custom script
bcp.exe executed under SYSTEM context with no user session; no user logs in during execution
bcp.exe hash mismatch with official Microsoft distribution
Confirmed C2 domain beaconing from AODB server to external host; traffic routed via DNS tunnel
Query logs show 14,728 passenger name records retrieved; no record of authorization
Backup job was not encrypted; exported data could have been copied to external media
bcp.exe process logged in via domain credentials; credential hash reuse detected
No alerts generated for bcp.exe or DNS tunneling traffic

actionsTaken: Confirmed bcp.exe is not part of standard AODB software suite
Isolated AODB server from network at 08:23
Initiated full forensic image of AODB server storage
Notified IT-Cyber and Ops Command via secure channel
recommendations: Immediately revoke all domain credentials due to compromise
Notify Legal/Compliance and PIO for breach reporting obligations
Begin passenger notification protocol under NCIA Incident Response Policy
Conduct full network-wide credential rotation and MFA enforcement
fields.photosNote: 3 attached: IMG_20261022-001 (bcp.exe process trace), IMG_20261022-002 (AODB export logs), IMG_20261022-003 (DNS tunneling packet capture) — all in .pdf format

instructorNote: This inject confirms the attacker has had long-term access to passenger data and flight operations. Watch for the legal team to initiate breach notification planning and for ops to assess passenger impact.
